This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a soft-tissue mass.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

content.thinking: I'm studying the leg image, locating the bone's marrow and tracing the bright mass wrapping around its left side, noting the coordinates of several marked points within that bright region in both panels.

content.text:
The tumour is the large, bright, lobulated mass on the image-left side of the dark bone, wrapping around it. Its centre is at roughly (1275, 440) in the right panel. Mark 506 sits at about (1275, 442), almost exactly on that centre. The nearby marks 514, 458, 465, 485 and 497 also fall inside the mass but nearer its edges.

ANSWER: 506
